label: Time-zero analysis set
text: PITFALL: Selecting cases using information from after time zero (for example only cases with an assessed week-16 visit, or cases outside the registry's time-zero analysis set) causes selection or immortal-time bias. CHECK: Restrict to analysis_set==1 and confirm that eligibility, therapy_class and covariates are all fixed at time_zero_day; tabulate analysis_set against therapy_class and assessed16. IF FOUND: Define the cohort only from baseline information, keep cases that were not assessed in the denominator, and never filter on assessed16. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12927355/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5124536/

label: Missing week-16 outcome needs IPCW/AIPW
text: PITFALL: The estimand is benefit 'as if all had an assessable week-16 visit' (a hypothetical estimand), so a complete-case analysis of benefit16 among assessed16==1 is biased when assessability depends on arm, toxicity or prognosis. CHECK: Model P(assessed16=1 | arm, baseline covariates) and compare assessment rates by arm, ECOG, tumor burden and tox_stop_8wk. IF FOUND: Estimate counterfactual risks by inverse-probability-of-censoring weighting combined with treatment weighting, or by doubly robust AIPW/g-computation over all analysis-set cases in the target population. Report the complete-case estimate only as a sensitivity analysis. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10228513/ ; https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.5643

label: Post-baseline variables in missingness model
text: PITFALL: Toxicity or discontinuation by week 8 (tox_stop_8wk) is post-treatment. Adjusting for it in the treatment or outcome model blocks part of the effect, but it may be the main driver of a missing week-16 assessment. CHECK: Cross-tabulate tox_stop_8wk by assessed16 within each arm. IF FOUND: Keep the treatment-effect model to baseline confounders only. If tox_stop is used to predict missingness, use a sequential (time-ordered) g-formula or IPCW in which tox_stop enters only the censoring model. Run a sensitivity analysis where it is excluded, and state the MAR assumption. SOURCE: https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9%2DR1_Step4_Guideline_2019_1203.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10228513/

label: Confounding by indication: marginal standardisation
text: PITFALL: In a tumor-board registry, choice of TXR1i versus SYS follows prognosis (ECOG, prior lines, prior resistance, tumor burden, lineage, site, calendar period), so a crude risk difference is confounded. A conditional odds ratio is also not the requested marginal risk difference. CHECK: Compute standardized mean differences of baseline covariates by therapy_class within the SV-positive target population before and after weighting (aim for |SMD|<0.1). IF FOUND: Use IPTW or AIPW/g-computation standardised to the SV-positive population and report the marginal risk difference in percentage points with a bootstrap CI. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4626409/ ; https://iqss.github.io/dss-ps/assessing.html

label: Positivity in small subgroup
text: PITFALL: In a small SV-positive subgroup, some covariate strata (site, period, lineage) may receive only one therapy, which gives extreme weights and unstable estimates. CHECK: Plot propensity score overlap by arm, report the minimum and maximum weight and the effective sample size per arm, and tabulate therapy by site and calendar_period within the target population. IF FOUND: Simplify the propensity score model, use stabilised or overlap-aware estimators, use AIPW rather than pure IPW, and report a truncation sensitivity analysis. If there is a structural zero, state the narrowed population rather than extrapolating. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12659692/ ; https://amertens.github.io/causal-learning-handbook/03-05-advanced-diagnostics.html

label: SV artifact calls in repeats
text: PITFALL: Long-read SV breakpoints in segmental duplications, low-complexity sequence, low-MAPQ regions or regions with long microhomology, or supported by few split molecules, are often false positives. Counting every reported breakpoint as SV-positive misclassifies the target population and dilutes the effect. CHECK: Inspect the distribution of mapq_median, segmental_dup_overlap, low_complexity_score, homology_bp, split_molecule_count relative to molecule_depth, and read_n50 among cases with breakpoint_topology != NONE. IF FOUND: Apply pre-specified QC filters before classifying cases (for example minimum supporting molecules scaled to depth, adequate MAPQ, no SD overlap) and run a sensitivity analysis with stricter or looser filters. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9845341/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11208083/

label: SV present is not target activation
text: PITFALL: Only a minority of SVs change expression of nearby genes. The target population is SV-driven TXR1 activation, which needs a mechanism (a promoter/enhancer-facing topology, P2T in this registry) plus functional evidence: allele-specific expression from the rearranged haplotype and overexpression. INV/D2T or distant junctions are likely passengers. CHECK: Cross-tabulate breakpoint_topology with breakpoint_distance_kb, target_ase_alt_fraction, phase_consistency, phase_linked_reads and txr1_log_tpm. IF FOUND: Define target-positive cases by topology + QC + haplotype-consistent ASE (and proximity), not by 'any SV' and not by expression alone. Report how many cases each rule admits and test the sensitivity of the estimate to the rule. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05504-4 ; https://aacrjournals.org/bloodcancerdiscov/article/6/4/343/763152/Enhancer-Hijacking-Discovery-in-Acute-Myeloid

label: High TXR1 expression is confounded by lineage/batch
text: PITFALL: TXR1 expression correlates with a lineage program (lineage_marker_log_tpm, lineage_class) and may vary with expression_batch, library size and RNA quality. Defining target activation by high TXR1 TPM therefore selects on lineage or batch rather than SV-driven activation, and lineage may itself be prognostic. CHECK: Regress txr1_log_tpm on lineage marker, housekeeping, batch, purity and rna_quality, and see whether SV-positive (P2T) cases remain outliers on the residual. IF FOUND: Use lineage- and batch-adjusted expression (residuals) as supporting evidence only, and adjust for lineage_class as a confounder in the effect model. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4107031/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9508766/

label: Purity and copy number when reading SV fractions
text: PITFALL: The raw alt_molecule_fraction or ASE fraction depends on tumor purity, local copy number and ploidy/WGD. A low raw fraction in a low-purity sample can be a clonal event, while a high fraction in an amplified segment can overstate support. CHECK: Compare alt_molecule_fraction with tumor_purity, local_total_copy, tumor_ploidy and wgd_flag, and compute an approximate purity- and copy-adjusted cancer-cell fraction. IF FOUND: Use purity- and copy-adjusted fractions, not raw fixed cutoffs, to call clonal target activation. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-14351-8 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13039-025-00718-3

label: Toxicity risk: standardise and use the DLR1 activity score
text: PITFALL: The 8-week toxicity risk under TXR1i in the target population is a counterfactual risk. A crude rate among treated SV-positive cases is biased if treated cases differ from the whole target population, for example in germline DLR1 metabolism (a likely toxicity modifier), age or ECOG. CHECK: Map dlr1_hap1/hap2 to an activity score by summing allele activity values from dlr1_allele_table (CPIC convention), flag cases with low dlr1_call_confidence, and compare the activity-score distribution between treated cases and all target cases. IF FOUND: Estimate toxicity risk with g-computation/IPTW standardised to the whole SV-positive population, include the activity score (with a sensitivity analysis for low-confidence calls) and keep all treated cases in the denominator. SOURCE: https://pharmcat.clinpgx.org/methods/Matching-Recommendations/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cpicpgx/cpic-sop/main/CPIC%20Pharmacogene%20Curation%20SOP.pdf

label: interchromosomal phase unknown
text: PITFALL: The h1/h2 labels in phased local-ancestry output are only consistent within a chromosome; phase between chromosomes is unknown, so 'h1' on chr1 and 'h1' on chr2 need not come from the same parent, and pooling by label mixes the two parents. CHECK: Per chromosome, compute the ancestry-A fraction of h1 and h2 over called span and see whether the higher-A haplotype is always labelled the same; also look at whether one haplotype per chromosome is near-pure (a sign of a recently or un-admixed parent). IF FOUND: Assign each chromosome's haplotypes to parent1/parent2 by a stated rule (e.g. by A fraction per chromosome, or a likelihood/EM over the 2^(n-1) assignments), report that this rule is assumed, and check how much the answer changes under other assignments; PAPI avoids this by modelling unphased ancestry with a binomial model on homozygous-ancestry regions. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/

label: spurious short tracts inflate t
text: PITFALL: Short, low-confidence ancestry tracts (low posterior, high low_complexity_frac) are often miscalls; each one adds two spurious ancestry junctions and pushes the admixture-time estimate up a lot. CHECK: Tabulate tract length against the posterior and low_complexity_frac columns; count tracts shorter than ~1-2 cM (0.01-0.02 Morgan) and see whether they are mostly low-posterior or high-low-complexity and sit between two flanking tracts of the same ancestry. IF FOUND: Before counting junctions, mask such tracts (treat as uncalled) or merge the flanking same-ancestry tracts across them, state the thresholds, and report how sensitive t is to them. Gravel warns that a length cutoff C needs a truncated likelihood and that many spurious short tracts still distort the longer ones. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

label: phase switch errors
text: PITFALL: Phase switch errors show up as reciprocal ancestry swaps between the two haplotypes at the same spot where ancestry is heterozygous (h1 goes A->B while h2 goes B->A); they create false junctions on both haplotypes and move ancestry from one parent to the other. CHECK: List breakpoints on h1 and h2 of each chromosome and flag pairs that coincide within ~1 cM (0.01 Morgan) and are reciprocal swaps. IF FOUND: Undo the swap ('unkink': flip the strands downstream of the switch, as Tractor does) before computing per-haplotype fractions and junction counts, or at least drop those junctions, and report how many were corrected. SOURCE: https://atkinson-lab.github.io/Tractor-tutorial/Recover.html ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2689842/

label: fraction over called span
text: PITFALL: The ancestry fraction must be computed over the called tract span, not over chromosome length; uncalled gaps (e.g. tracts that start at 0.03 M rather than 0, or holes between tracts) and any tracts you mask take ancestry out of both the numerator and the denominator. CHECK: Compare the summed called length per haplotype with the summed map_info length_morgan values, and list the gaps between consecutive tracts. IF FOUND: Use fraction_A = sum(length of A tracts) / sum(length of all called tracts kept) per haplotype, say whether masked low-confidence tracts are excluded, and do not count an ancestry change across an uncalled gap as a certain junction (or report t both with and without such changes). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/

label: censoring at chromosome ends
text: PITFALL: Tracts that touch a chromosome end or an uncalled gap are censored (their true length is longer), so the naive mean tract length or the 'number of tracts' per chromosome is biased; with a few chromosomes and a recent pulse, censored tracts are a large share of the data. CHECK: Count the tracts per haplotype whose start or end is the first or last called position of the chromosome. IF FOUND: Estimate t from the count of internal junctions (ancestry changes between adjacent called tracts, after merging same-ancestry neighbours) divided by called length, or use a censored-exponential likelihood; do not treat chromosome ends as junctions. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/ ; https://academic.oup.com/genetics/article/197/3/953/5935994

label: t to junction-rate formula
text: PITFALL: The way time t is turned into a junction rate decides the answer. Under the Markov pulse model a haploid lineage that had a pulse t generations ago with ancestry fraction m has junctions at expected density 2*t*m*(1-m) per Morgan (A tracts ~ Exp(t(1-m)), B tracts ~ Exp(t*m)); using the individual's average m instead of that haplotype's own m, or mixing up t with t-1 (whether t counts from the child or from the parent who transmitted the haplotype), changes t by 1 or more. CHECK: Write down the convention before estimating, and for each haplotype use its own m and its own called length L: t_hat = J / (2 m (1-m) L), with J the number of internal junctions. IF FOUND: Report t on the parent's time scale (PAPI defines parental admixture times; a parent from an unadmixed source has t of about 1 and a haplotype with no junctions), state whether a +/-1 offset was applied and why, and give a Poisson interval on J. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/

label: few junctions, non-exponential
text: PITFALL: For recent admixture (a few generations) the iid-exponential tract-length model is only an approximation (Liang and Nielsen), and a single individual gives only tens of junctions, so a fitted tract-length distribution is noisy and can lean on outlier long tracts. CHECK: Count the junctions per haplotype; if they are under ~30, the Poisson error on t is above ~20%. IF FOUND: Prefer the junction-count (method-of-moments) estimator, or a likelihood that handles finite chromosomes, over fitting a histogram of tract lengths; report a confidence interval (Poisson on J, or a bootstrap over chromosomes) and expect PAPI-like methods to underestimate t by about 1 generation when LAI merges short tracts. SOURCE: https://academic.oup.com/genetics/article/197/3/953/5935994 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/

label: merge same-ancestry neighbours
text: PITFALL: Adjacent called tracts with the same ancestry (split by the caller, or left after you mask a short miscall) are not ancestry junctions; counting every tract boundary as a switch inflates t. CHECK: Within each chromosome and haplotype, sort by start and count boundaries where anc is the same on both sides. IF FOUND: Merge same-ancestry neighbours (if the gap between them is small or zero) before counting junctions; count only A<->B changes. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/
